questions.question: What is the difference between type and interface in TypeScript? When should you use each?
questions.title: type vs interface in TypeScript — Differences & When to Use Each
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between type and interface in TypeScript? When should you use each?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** interface for object-shape extension/merging; type for unions, intersections, tuples, mapped types; declaration-merging differences.

**Classic weak answer:** Claiming one is always better than the other — they overlap heavily; guideline: prefer interface for object shapes, type for composition.

**Senior finish:** Mention declaration merging (interfaces only), union/intersection (type only), and that classes can implement both.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **type vs interface in TypeScript — Differences & When to Use Each** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the difference between type and interface in TypeScript? When should you use each?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **interface for object-shape extension/merging; type for unions, intersections, tuples, mapped types; declaration-merging differences**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Claiming one is always better than the other — they overlap heavily; guideline: prefer interface for object shapes, type for composition**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention declaration merging (interfaces only), union/intersection (type only), and that classes can implement both**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** interface for object-shape extension/merging; type for unions, intersections, tuples, mapped types; declaration-merging differences
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **claiming one is always better than the other — they overlap heavily; guideline: prefer interface for object shapes, type for composition** and what you do instead.

sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **interface for object-shape extension/merging; type for unions, intersections, tuples, mapped types; declaration-merging differences** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Claiming one is always better than the other — they overlap heavily; guideline: prefer interface for object shapes, type for composition** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention declaration merging (interfaces only), union/intersection (type only), and that classes can implement both**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: What is structural typing in TypeScript? How does it differ from nominal typing?
questions.title: Structural Typing in TypeScript — Duck Typing Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is structural typing in TypeScript? How does it differ from nominal typing?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** TS types are compared by shape (structural), not by name (nominal); enables duck typing; implications for branded/opaque types.

**Classic weak answer:** Assuming two classes with the same shape aren't assignable — they are, because TS is structural.

**Senior finish:** Introduce branded types (nominal-style) via intersection with a unique symbol to simulate nominal typing when needed.
